question: Can a class-balanced classifier on engineered trend and shift features beat a 1-nearest-neighbour template-matching baseline at recognising control chart patterns on the UCI Synthetic Control Chart dataset?
method: Stratified 70/30 split (seed 42); baseline 1-NN Euclidean on raw series; improved class-balanced RBF SVM on standardized raw + engineered features with CV-selected C and gamma; macro-F1 on test.

dataset.name: UCI Synthetic Control Chart Time Series

baseline: 1-nearest-neighbour template matcher, Euclidean distance on raw 60-point series (stand-in for the paper's unstated pattern-matching method)
improved: class-balanced RBF SVM on standardized raw series plus engineered linear slope, segment means, shift magnitude, variance and peak-to-peak range; C and gamma chosen by stratified 5-fold CV on training data only
notes: Single stratified split; test set used once for each model. Both models are deterministic here (std 0). The improved model was changed from class-balanced LightGBM (which CV showed at ~0.971 macro-F1, below the 1-NN baseline) to an RBF SVM with standardized features, a model family that is well suited to small, low-dimensional time-series data. Class labels are inferred from the file's row order (100 rows per class). With 180 test series, differences of a few samples are noisy. The paper's own method and results are not specified, so this is not a replication.
